claim: A column of heat shimmer rises across the surface — the image wavering through refracting air, like asphalt in August. Content is refracted, never replaced.

q1_defects.answer: No placeholder-slab and no blur/clipping/broken-frame — the real card (brass header bar, grey body rows, blue accent dot) is preserved and tack-sharp in every frame. BUT two real defects: (a) the distortion is near-invisible and confined to a faint wavy notch on the TOP EDGE of the single brightest element (the brass bar) — the grey body rows show zero displacement; (b) controls are effectively dead — metrics report changed:false on all five, and duration is genuinely indistinguishable low-vs-high to the eye.
evidence: metrics: play-1/play-2 frameDeltaMag=0.02, play-3=0.05 — near-zero inter-frame motion
metrics: all 5 controls changed=false (duration pixelDiff meanAbsDiff=0.051 changedFrac=0.0003; amplitude 0.015/0.0005)

q2_reads_as.answer: No — it does not read as the claim at premium quality. The claim promises a column of heat shimmer rising across the whole surface, the image wavering like asphalt in August. What renders is a tiny refraction notch on the top edge of one brass bar; the bulk of the card (grey rows) does not waver at all. It reads as a faint accidental edge-wobble, not heat haze. This outclasses nothing.
evidence: metrics: effSat~0.09 meanLuma=16.7 stdev=24.9 unchanged across all play frames — no shimmer signal

q3_discoverable.answer: No — the effect is not obvious. The idle card invites it (clean, legible), but the active frames are so close to idle that a first-time user would not notice anything is happening. The wobble is sub-perceptual except on the brass bar's top edge.

q4_responsive.answer: Mostly no. amplitude and distortionScale produce a faintly more visible ripple on the brass-bar edge at high vs low, but it is barely perceptible; duration, columnWidth, and riseSpeed are visually dead. The harness scores changed=false on all five controls.
evidence: metrics: duration changedFrac=0.0003, columnWidth changedFrac=0, riseSpeed changedFrac=0.0011 — all changed=false

q5_net.answer: ANNOYED — content preservation and sharpness are fine, but the effect fails the load-bearing reads-as-claim test (no surface-wide heat shimmer; only a faint single-bar edge wobble) and the controls-live test (duration/columnWidth/riseSpeed visually dead). Under-powered and accidental-looking, not premium.
evidence: metrics: all 5 controls changed=false; play frameDeltaMag<=0.05

mustFix.issue: Effect does not read as the claim: no column of heat shimmer rising across the surface and no whole-image wavering. Distortion is confined to a faint notch on the top edge of the brass header bar; the grey body rows (bulk of the card) show no displacement at all. It reads as an accidental edge-wobble, not asphalt-in-August heat haze.
mustFix.evidence: heat-haze-refract/after/play-3.png and control-distortionScale-high.png show ripple only on the brass-bar top edge; grey rows unchanged vs idle.png. metrics: play frameDeltaMag<=0.05, effSat/meanLuma/stdev identical across all play frames.

mustFix.issue: Controls are not live. Harness reports changed=false on all five (duration changedFrac=0.0003, columnWidth changedFrac=0, riseSpeed changedFrac=0.0011). Visually, duration/columnWidth/riseSpeed low-vs-high frames are indistinguishable; amplitude/distortionScale differ only sub-perceptibly. A premium primitive must show clear low-to-high response.
mustFix.evidence: control-duration-low.png vs control-duration-high.png are indistinguishable; metrics controls[] all report changed=false.

mustFix.issue: Effect strength is below the discoverability floor — a first-time user would not perceive that anything is animating. frameDeltaMag of 0.02-0.05 between play frames means the surface is effectively static; the heat haze needs to be dialed up substantially to read at premium 4K-motion-graphics quality.
mustFix.evidence: idle.png vs play-1.png/play-2.png are near-identical; metrics: play-1/2 frameDeltaMag=0.02.

flags.note: Positive: no placeholder-slab defect and no blur — the real card look (brass header, grey rows, blue accent dot) is preserved and tack-sharp. The W3 texture-preserving invariant is satisfied; the failure is purely in effect strength/readability, not in content substitution.
flags.evidence: idle.png, play-1.png, all control frames all show the genuine card content sharp and intact.

flags.note: When the fix lands, the refraction should distort the entire column of content (grey rows included), not just the brightest bar's top edge — currently the displacement appears to read only where there is a high-contrast horizontal edge.
flags.evidence: control-amplitude-high.png shows wobble on the brass bar but the three grey rows below remain perfectly straight.
